title: Python frozenset: Immutable Sets
learningObjectives: Explain how a frozenset differs from a regular set.
Create a frozenset from an iterable.
Use membership tests and set operations with frozensets.
Explain why a frozenset can be used as a dictionary key or as a member of another set when its elements are hashable.
Recognize that frozensets do not support mutating methods such as add() or remove().

understand.concept: A frozenset is an immutable set. It stores unique hashable elements and supports membership tests and non-mutating set operations such as union, intersection and difference. Unlike a regular set, a frozenset cannot be changed after creation: methods such as add(), remove(), discard() and clear() are not available. A frozenset is hashable when its elements are hashable, so it can be used as a dictionary key or as a member of another set.
understand.whyItMatters: Immutable sets are useful when a collection of unique values must remain stable, such as a key representing a group of permissions or a member in a set of combinations.
understand.analogy: A regular set is a whiteboard list that can be edited; a frozenset is a signed snapshot whose membership cannot be changed.
understand.analogyLimit: Python hashability and equality rules are more precise than the idea of a signed snapshot.
understand.summary: Use frozenset() for immutable unique collections. It supports read-only set operations but not in-place mutation.

explain.narrative:
## Create a frozenset
Use `frozenset(iterable)` to create an immutable set. Duplicate values are removed and the order is not guaranteed.

## Operations
Frozensets support membership checks, iteration, subset/superset tests and non-mutating operations such as union, intersection and difference. These operations return set-like results without modifying the original frozenset.

## Immutability and hashability
A frozenset has no add(), remove() or clear() method. When all its elements are hashable, it can itself be used as a dictionary key or stored inside another set.

examples.title: Create a frozenset
examples.code:
values = frozenset([1, 2, 2, 3])
print(len(values))
print(2 in values)
examples.explanation: frozenset removes duplicates and supports membership tests.

examples.title: Build a frozenset from a string
examples.explanation: A string is iterable, so its unique characters become frozenset members.

examples.title: Use a non-mutating set operation
examples.code:
required = frozenset({'read', 'write'})
extra = required.union({'execute'})
print(sorted(required))
print(sorted(extra))
examples.explanation: union returns a new set-like result and leaves the original frozenset unchanged.

examples.title: Use a frozenset as a dictionary key
examples.explanation: A frozenset of hashable values is hashable and can be used as a dictionary key.

examples.title: Store a frozenset inside another set
examples.explanation: Frozensets are hashable when their elements are hashable, so they can be members of another set.

practise.guidedTask: Create a frozenset of unique course permissions, test membership, and compare it with the result of a union operation while confirming that the original is unchanged.
practise.independentTask: Represent role permissions with frozensets and use them as dictionary keys. Add a check that distinguishes a mutable set from an immutable frozenset.
hints: Do not rely on frozenset iteration order when printing.
Use sorted() when deterministic display order is required.
Use union(), intersection() and difference() for non-mutating operations.
A frozenset can be a dictionary key only when all its members are hashable.
practise.challenge: Build a permission lookup where each role is represented by a frozenset and the mapping uses those frozensets as keys; demonstrate membership and set comparison without mutation.
validationCriteria: The lesson correctly distinguishes set and frozenset mutability.
Non-mutating operations leave the original frozenset unchanged.
Dictionary-key and nested-set examples execute correctly.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between set and frozenset?
questions.explanation: A frozenset cannot be changed after it is created.

questions.prompt: Which expression creates an immutable set from values?
questions.explanation: The built-in frozenset() constructor creates an immutable set.

questions.prompt: Which operation is not available for a frozenset?
questions.explanation: frozenset has no mutating add() method.

questions.prompt: Why can a frozenset be used as a dictionary key?
questions.answer: It is hashable when all its elements are hashable
